title: Single-photon time qubit: Quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time
abstract: Treating the arrow of time as a controllable quantum variable rather than a fixed external parameter is a central challenge in quantum physics. Recently, Bloch~\cite{Bloch2025} proposed the theoretical concept of a \emph{time qubit}, a two-level control space $\mathcal{H}_T=\mathrm{span}\{\ket{+},\ket{-}\}$ that selects between opposite Hamiltonian evolutions $\hat{H}_{\pm}=\hat{H}_0\pm\hat{V}$, but this paradigm has remained experimentally unrealized. Here we formulate the quantum-optical theory of a single-photon time qubit---uncovering quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time---and experimentally probe and validate its predictions using phase-resolved single-photon interferometry from two coherently seeded entangled nonlinear biphoton sources~\cite{Lee2018,Yoon2021}. First, we show theoretically and verify experimentally that a controlled $π$ pump--seed phase inversion during pair creation from the quantum vacuum flips the stimulated displacement generator $\hat{V}\to -\hat{V}$ on top of the spontaneous two-mode squeezing background $\hat{H}_0$, reversing the stimulated evolution time [$\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},-}(t)=\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},+}(-t)$] and enabling universal single-qubit $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ control and postselection-free first-order tomography on the temporal Bloch sphere. Second, we prove that spontaneous idler vacuum fluctuations record complete which-branch (temporal-direction) information whereas the shared coherent seed erases it without cascading or aligning the idler beams, establishing an exact wave--particle complementarity law $|\bm{r}|=\mathcal{V}=|α|^2/(1+|α|^2)$ for the purity of the arrow of time and enabling direct first-order measurement of the Loschmidt time-reversal echo.
summary: This paper proposes and experimentally validates a single-photon time qubit by controlling the Hamiltonian evolution using quantum vacuum effects in an interferometric setup. The key achievements include demonstrating time-reversal symmetry control, achieving universal single-qubit quantum gate operations, and establishing a fundamental complementarity law linking wave and particle descriptions of time evolution.
main_problem: The central challenge is treating the arrow of time as a controllable quantum variable rather than a fixed external parameter, which requires realizing a physical time qubit.
main_result: The authors demonstrate universal single-qubit SU(2) control over a time qubit using quantum-vacuum control, and establish an exact wave-particle complementarity law for the arrow of time.
method: The work combines theoretical quantum-optical modeling with experimental validation using phase-resolved single-photon interferometry from coherently seeded entangled nonlinear biphoton sources.
model_or_system: The system is a single-photon time qubit realized in a hybrid nonlinear-linear interferometer architecture. The dynamics are governed by a controlled Hamiltonian $\hat{H} \propto \hat{H}_0 \pm \hat{V}$, where $\hat{H}_0$ is the spontaneous squeezing background and $\hat{V}$ is the stimulated displacement generator.
key_observables: Time-parity fringes, Loschmidt time-reversal echo amplitude $L(t)$, and the complementarity law $|r| = V = |\alpha|^2/(1+|\alpha|^2)$.
important_parameters: The control mechanism relies on a controlled $\pi$ pump–seed phase inversion to flip $\hat{V} 	o -\hat{V}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to map local supermodes onto isomorphic target modes to yield the controlled Hamiltonian, and that the ENBS platform provides postselection-free measurement.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the ENBS interferometer architecture. Figure 2 shows the Temporal Bloch-sphere representation and the interferometric readout. Figure 4 shows open-loop PZT ramp scans of single-photon interference fringes.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the theoretical framework of the time qubit and its connection to vacuum control. It then details the experimental realization using ENBS interferometry to achieve time reversal and SU(2) control. Finally, it proves the wave-particle complementarity law and discusses scaling to multi-qubit and error-correcting regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fundamental questions at the intersection of quantum foundations (arrow of time) and quantum computation by implementing a novel, controllable quantum resource (the time qubit) using photonic platforms.
